headline: Multi-omics profiling nominates prognostic and niche-linked markers in solid tumors
label: Multi Omics Cancer Biomarker Discovery
summary: Single-cell, bulk and spatial transcriptomes combined with machine learning now nominate candidate biomarkers lacking clinical validation.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the layering of single-cell, bulk and spatial transcriptomic data with computational modelling to derive prognostic signatures and map tumor-microenvironment states, mostly in solid tumors. Several studies focus on metabolic programs: glycolytic heterogeneity and spatial niche remodeling in colorectal cancer, and lactate-glycolysis programs linked to neutrophil-enriched immune remodeling in lung adenocarcinoma. Other items pair glutamine metabolism, NNMT-associated metabolic-immune co-activation, or interferon-response epithelial states with prognostic modelling. Public resources are pooled for meta-analysis, including 54 scRNA-seq and 88 bulk RNA-seq datasets in glioblastoma. What is newer is the explicit niche-level framing that links metabolic programs to immune remodeling. Candidate markers such as the five-gene TFPI-associated signature and MAP1LC3A remain computationally derived, and these items do not establish their clinical utility.
